title: Review check becomes a reusable workflow
summary: The review check's job logic moves out of osf's own `review.yml` into a new reusable workflow, `review-check.yml`, which any repository can call. `review.yml` shrinks to a single caller job that passes five inputs — the pinned osf commit, the osf repository, the runner label, the verifier app id and `allow-forks` — and grants the union of the permissions the called jobs need. The build job now checks out osf at the pinned `osf-ref` into `osf-src` (read-only) and writes to a separate `build-out`, instead of building the base checkout in place. Fork review moves from the `OSF_REVIEW_FORKS` repository variable read inside the workflow to an `allow-forks` input the caller supplies. The workflow tests are extended to cover both files, the stable input list, and the caller's thinness.

lanes.label: Caller workflow
lanes.subtitle: pull_request_target, base branch
lanes.summary: The workflow GitHub reads from the base branch. It holds no step of its own; it only calls the reusable workflow and passes inputs.

lanes.label: Reusable review check
lanes.subtitle: review-check.yml, workflow_call
lanes.summary: Every job of the review check: build, the three reviewer jobs, the deciding job, and the fork-disabled job. Called by osf's own review.yml and by adopters.

lanes.label: Runner and containers
lanes.subtitle: docker run, pinned image
lanes.summary: The GitHub runner and the pinned devcontainer image each job runs osf in. The build job now mounts the pinned osf checkout read-only and writes to a separate build-out.

lanes.label: External services
lanes.subtitle: GitHub, registries, providers
lanes.summary: The hosts each job is allowed to reach: GitHub, ghcr.io, crates.io, and one model provider per reviewer job.

nodes.label: review.yml
nodes.subtitle: pull_request_target caller
nodes.summary: osf's own caller. It keeps the pull_request_target trigger and the read-only permissions, and replaces every job with one `uses: ./.github/workflows/review-check.yml` job that passes osf-repository, osf-ref (the base commit), runs-on, verifier-app-id and allow-forks.

nodes.label: review-check.yml
nodes.subtitle: workflow_call, five inputs
nodes.summary: The new reusable workflow. It declares only `workflow_call`, takes five inputs and no secret, and holds every job the review check runs. Its header states that the caller must be a pull_request_target workflow and that the called workflow runs from the commit its caller names.

nodes.label: build job
nodes.subtitle: no secret, read-only token
nodes.summary: Checks out osf at the pinned osf-ref into osf-src, refuses any osf-ref that is not a full 40-character SHA, refuses any event but pull_request_target, builds the release binary into build-out, and runs `osf review work-item` to find the issue the pull request names. It holds no provider key and needs no environment.

nodes.label: reviewer jobs
nodes.subtitle: codex, claude, opencode
nodes.summary: One job per reviewer, each with only its own provider key from the `review` environment (or `fork-review` for a fork) and an egress allow-list of its provider's hosts. Each checks out the caller's base and the pull request's head as data, downloads the built osf, and runs `osf review run --reviewer <name> --if-enabled`.

nodes.label: review job
nodes.subtitle: collects, decides, posts
nodes.summary: The last job. It downloads every reviewer's saved answers, mints the verifier app's token with the verifier-app-id input, and runs `osf review reduce` to decide and post. It runs even when a reviewer job failed, and a reviewer with no saved answers counts as could-not-run.

nodes.label: review-fork-disabled
nodes.subtitle: fails loudly
nodes.summary: Runs when the pull request comes from a fork and the caller did not pass allow-forks. It has no permissions and no allowed endpoints, and fails rather than skipping, so an unconfigured fork review cannot pass the check.

nodes.label: GitHub runner
nodes.subtitle: Linux with Docker
nodes.summary: The runner named by the runs-on input. Every job asserts it is Linux before running any docker command, because the steps assume docker run and Unix paths such as /base and /pr.

nodes.label: devcontainer image
nodes.subtitle: pinned by digest
nodes.summary: The one image every job runs, named once by digest in REVIEW_IMAGE and never by a moving tag. It carries the pinned Rust toolchain and the reviewer tools, including codex 0.161.0, which the codex job verifies.

nodes.label: osf-src checkout
nodes.subtitle: read-only, pinned commit
nodes.summary: The build job's checkout of osf at osf-ref, mounted read-only at /osf-src. It replaces the old writable base mount, so the build can no longer write into the tree it compiles.

nodes.label: build-out
nodes.subtitle: writable, runner-owned
nodes.summary: The folder the build writes to, mounted writable at /build-out and owned by the runner user. CARGO_HOME and CARGO_TARGET_DIR point inside it, and the release binary is uploaded from it as the osf-binary artifact.

nodes.label: base and pr checkouts
nodes.subtitle: read-only data
nodes.summary: The caller's base branch, which holds the trusted configuration, and the pull request's head, which is data only. Both are mounted read-only into the reviewer and deciding containers, with a generated gitconfig marking them safe directories.

nodes.label: GitHub API
nodes.subtitle: issues, pull requests, checks
nodes.summary: Read by the build job's read-only token to find the work item, and written by the deciding job through the verifier app's token to post the review.

nodes.label: ghcr.io
nodes.subtitle: image registry
nodes.summary: Every job logs in with its own token and pulls the pinned devcontainer image by digest.

nodes.label: crates.io
nodes.subtitle: cargo registry
nodes.summary: Reached only by the build job, which compiles osf from the pinned commit with no cache.

nodes.label: model providers
nodes.subtitle: one host per reviewer
nodes.summary: Each reviewer job's egress allow-list holds only its own provider's hosts: api.openai.com and chatgpt.com for codex, api.anthropic.com for claude, openrouter.ai and models.opencode.ai for opencode.

nodes.label: review_workflow.rs
nodes.subtitle: checks both files
nodes.summary: Reads review-check.yml as the workflow under test and review.yml as the caller. New tests pin the stable input list, forbid workflow_call secrets and `vars.` reads, require the pinned-SHA checkout and the pull_request_target guard, and assert the caller is thin and passes exactly the declared inputs.

nodes.label: development.md
nodes.subtitle: how to call the check
nodes.summary: Adds a section documenting the caller shape, the five inputs, why no secret is a workflow_call secret, what is stable, and the organisation setting a private factory repo needs to share the workflow.

nodes.label: ADR 0016
nodes.subtitle: the review check
nodes.summary: Records that review.yml now holds no job of its own and calls the reusable workflow, which an adopter's repository can call too.

edges.label: uses, five inputs
edges.summary: The caller names the reusable workflow by a local path, which GitHub reads at the same base commit, and passes osf-ref as the pull request's base commit.
The reusable workflow's first job. It needs no environment and holds no provider key.

edges.label: osf-binary, work-item
edges.summary: The build job uploads the release binary and the work item as artifacts; each reviewer job downloads both.

edges.label: review-run-*.json
edges.summary: Each reviewer job uploads its saved answers even when it failed; the deciding job downloads every review-run-* artifact and passes them to `osf review reduce`.
When the head is a fork and allow-forks is false, this job fails the check instead of letting it pass unconfigured.

edges.label: read-only
edges.summary: The build job checks out osf at the pinned osf-ref and mounts it read-only at /osf-src.

edges.label: cargo build
edges.summary: cargo build writes the release binary and its caches into the runner-owned build-out folder.

edges.label: read-only
edges.summary: Reviewer jobs mount the caller's base and the pull request's head read-only, so the pull request's tree is only ever data.

edges.label: read-only
edges.summary: The deciding job mounts the same two trees read-only while it checks findings against the pull request's files.

edges.label: read-only token
edges.summary: The build job's token reads issues and pull requests only, to find the work item the pull request names.

edges.label: verifier app token
edges.summary: The deciding job alone mints the verifier app's token, with pull-requests write, and posts the review.

edges.label: docker login
edges.summary: Every job logs in to ghcr.io with its own token and pulls the image pinned by digest.

edges.label: cargo fetch
edges.summary: The build job's egress allow-list includes the crates.io hosts, because it compiles osf with no cache.

edges.label: one key each
edges.summary: Each reviewer job passes only its own provider's key into the container and allows only that provider's hosts out.
The tests read review-check.yml as the workflow under test and assert its input list, its pinned checkout and its event guard.
The tests read review.yml as the caller and assert it is thin, passes exactly the declared inputs, and grants no write permission.
The guide documents each input, the caller shape and what is stable; a test asserts the guide names every stable input.

flows.title: One review run through the reusable check
flows.summary: A pull request event reaches the caller, which calls the reusable workflow. The build job compiles the pinned osf and finds the work item; each reviewer job runs its own reviewer against the pull request's tree as data; the deciding job collects the answers and posts the review.

views.summary: The caller, the reusable workflow's jobs, the runner and containers they use, and the external hosts they reach.

views.title: Build job internals
views.summary: What the build job does with the pinned osf checkout, the writable build-out, and the read-only token that finds the work item.

views.title: Caller contract
views.summary: The thin caller, the reusable workflow it names, and the tests and guide that pin the input list.

steps.heading: The caller only calls
steps.body: review.yml keeps the pull_request_target trigger and drops every job.

detail.text: The caller review.yml names the reusable workflow by a local path and passes osf-ref as the base commit.

steps.heading: Build the pinned osf
steps.body: The build job checks out osf at osf-ref and compiles it into build-out.

detail.text: The pinned checkout is mounted read-only and the build writes only to the runner-owned build-out folder.

steps.heading: Each reviewer runs alone
steps.body: Three reviewer jobs each hold one provider key and one provider's hosts.

detail.text: Each reviewer jobs mount the caller's base and the pull request's head read-only, so the tree is data.

steps.heading: One job decides and posts
steps.body: The last job collects every saved answer and mints the verifier token.

detail.text: The deciding job alone mints the verifier app's token and posts the review.
The build job hands the binary and work item to the reviewer jobs, which hand their saved answers to the deciding job.
